sources.title: AI Engineering
sources.label: AI
sources.summary: Complete source curriculum: phases, manuals, code, labs, projects, certifications, paths, cheat sheets, and glossary.

sections.title: Phase 00 · Setup & Tooling
sections.tagline: Get your environment ready for everything that follows.

subsections.title: Dev Environment
subsections.description: Your tools shape your thinking. Set them up once, set them up right.

subsections.title: Git & Collaboration
subsections.description: Version control is not optional. Every experiment, every model, every lesson you build here gets tracked.

subsections.title: GPU Setup & Cloud
subsections.description: Training on CPU is fine for learning. Training for real needs a GPU.

subsections.title: APIs & Keys
subsections.description: Every AI API works the same way: send a request, get a response. The details change, the pattern doesn't.

subsections.title: Jupyter Notebooks
subsections.description: Notebooks are the lab bench of AI engineering. You prototype here, then move what works into production.

subsections.title: Python Environments
subsections.description: Dependency hell is real. Virtual environments are the cure.

subsections.title: Docker for AI
subsections.description: Containers make "works on my machine" a thing of the past.

subsections.title: Editor Setup
subsections.description: Your editor is your co-pilot. Configure it once so it stays out of your way and starts pulling its weight.

subsections.title: Data Management
subsections.description: Data is the fuel. How you manage it determines how fast you go.

subsections.title: Terminal & Shell
subsections.description: The terminal is where AI engineers live. Get comfortable here.

subsections.title: Linux for AI
subsections.description: Most AI runs on Linux. You need to know enough to not be stuck.

subsections.title: Debugging & Profiling
subsections.description: The worst AI bugs don't crash. They train silently on garbage and report a beautiful loss curve.

subsections.title: Python for AI Engineering
subsections.description: Most code in this course uses the same small set of Python idioms. Learn that set here, before the math and model lessons depend on it.

sections.title: Phase 01 · Math Foundations
sections.tagline: The intuition behind every AI algorithm, through code.

subsections.title: Linear Algebra Intuition
subsections.description: Every AI model is just matrix math wearing a fancy hat.

subsections.title: Vectors, Matrices & Operations
subsections.description: Every neural network is just matrix multiplication with extra steps.

subsections.title: Matrix Transformations & Eigenvalues
subsections.description: A matrix is a machine that reshapes space. Learn what it does to every point, and you understand the whole transformation.

subsections.title: Calculus for ML: Derivatives & Gradients
subsections.description: Derivatives tell you which way is downhill. That is all a neural network needs to learn.

subsections.title: Chain Rule & Automatic Differentiation
subsections.description: The chain rule is the engine behind every neural network that learns.

subsections.title: Probability & Distributions
subsections.description: Probability is the language AI uses to express uncertainty.

subsections.title: Bayes' Theorem & Statistical Thinking
subsections.description: Probability is about what you expect. Bayes' theorem is about what you learn.

subsections.title: Optimization: Gradient Descent Family
subsections.description: Training a neural network is nothing more than finding the bottom of a valley.

subsections.title: Information Theory: Entropy, KL Divergence
subsections.description: Information theory measures surprise. Loss functions are built on it.

subsections.title: Dimensionality Reduction: PCA, t-SNE, UMAP
subsections.description: High-dimensional data has structure. You find it by looking from the right angle.

subsections.title: Singular Value Decomposition
subsections.description: SVD is the Swiss Army knife of linear algebra. Every matrix has one. Every data scientist needs one.

subsections.title: Tensor Operations
subsections.description: Tensors are the common language between data and deep learning. Every image, every sentence, every gradient flows through them.

subsections.title: Numerical Stability
subsections.description: Floating point is a leaky abstraction. It will bite you during training, and you will not see it coming.

subsections.title: Norms & Distances
subsections.description: Your distance function defines what "similar" means. Choose wrong and everything downstream breaks.

subsections.title: Statistics for ML
subsections.description: Statistics is how you know if your model actually works or just got lucky.

subsections.title: Sampling Methods
subsections.description: Sampling is how AI explores the space of possibilities.

subsections.title: Linear Systems
subsections.description: Solving $Ax = b$ is the oldest problem in mathematics that still runs your neural network.

subsections.title: Convex Optimization
subsections.description: Convex problems have one valley. Neural networks have millions. Knowing the difference matters.

subsections.title: Complex Numbers for AI
subsections.description: The square root of -1 is not imaginary. It is the key to rotations, frequencies, and half of signal processing.

subsections.title: The Fourier Transform
subsections.description: Every signal is a sum of sine waves. The Fourier transform tells you which ones.

subsections.title: Graph Theory for ML
subsections.description: Graphs are the data structure of relationships. If your data has connections, you need graph theory.

subsections.title: Stochastic Processes
subsections.description: Randomness with structure. The math behind random walks, Markov chains, and diffusion models.

sections.title: Phase 02 · ML Fundamentals
sections.tagline: Classical ML — still the backbone of most production AI.

subsections.title: What Is Machine Learning
subsections.description: Machine learning is teaching computers to find patterns in data instead of writing rules by hand.

subsections.title: Linear Regression from Scratch
subsections.description: Linear regression draws the best straight line through your data. It is the "hello world" of machine learning.

subsections.title: Logistic Regression & Classification
subsections.description: Logistic regression bends a straight line into an S-curve to answer yes-or-no questions with probabilities.

subsections.title: Decision Trees & Random Forests
subsections.description: A decision tree is just a flowchart. But a forest of them is one of the most powerful tools in ML.

subsections.title: Support Vector Machines
subsections.description: Find the widest street between two classes. That is the entire idea.

subsections.title: KNN & Distance Metrics
subsections.description: Store everything. Predict by looking at your neighbors. The simplest algorithm that actually works.

subsections.title: Unsupervised Learning: K-Means, DBSCAN
subsections.description: No labels, no teacher. The algorithm finds structure on its own.

subsections.title: Feature Engineering & Selection
subsections.description: A good feature is worth a thousand data points.

subsections.title: Model Evaluation: Metrics, Cross-Validation
subsections.description: A model is only as good as the way you measure it.

subsections.title: Bias, Variance & the Learning Curve
subsections.description: Every model error comes from one of three sources: bias, variance, or noise. You can only control the first two.

subsections.title: Ensemble Methods: Boosting, Bagging, Stacking
subsections.description: A group of weak learners, combined correctly, becomes a strong learner. This is not a metaphor. It is a theorem.

subsections.title: Hyperparameter Tuning
subsections.description: Hyperparameters are the knobs you turn before training starts. Turning them well is the difference between a mediocre model and a great one.

subsections.title: ML Pipelines & Experiment Tracking
subsections.description: A model is not a product. A pipeline is. The pipeline is everything from raw data to deployed prediction, and every step must be reproducible.

subsections.title: Naive Bayes
subsections.description: The "naive" assumption is wrong, and it works anyway. That's the beauty of it.

subsections.title: Time Series Fundamentals
subsections.description: Past performance does predict future results -- if you check for stationarity first.

subsections.title: Anomaly Detection
subsections.description: Normal is easy to define. Abnormal is whatever doesn't fit.

subsections.title: Handling Imbalanced Data
subsections.description: When 99% of your data is "normal," accuracy is a lie.

subsections.title: Feature Selection
subsections.description: More features is not better. The right features is better.

subsections.title: ML System Design — From Problem to Deployed Model
subsections.description: A model is one part of a system. The design decides what the model predicts, who acts on it, what it costs, and what happens when it fails.

subsections.title: Monitoring Models in Production — Data Drift and Concept Drift
subsections.description: A deployed model fails without an error message. It keeps returning scores while the world moves away from its training data, and only monitoring shows the gap.

subsections.title: Feature Stores and Training-Serving Skew
subsections.description: A feature has one definition and two readers. Training reads its history as of each label time, and serving reads its latest value. When the two readers disagree, the model sees…

sections.title: Phase 03 · Deep Learning Core
sections.tagline: Neural networks from first principles. No frameworks until you build one.

subsections.title: The Perceptron: Where It All Started
subsections.description: The perceptron is the atom of neural networks. Split it open and you find weights, a bias, and a decision.

subsections.title: Multi-Layer Networks & Forward Pass
subsections.description: One neuron draws a line. Stack them, and you can draw anything.

subsections.title: Backpropagation from Scratch
subsections.description: Backpropagation is the algorithm that makes learning possible. Without it, neural networks are just expensive random number generators.

subsections.title: Activation Functions: ReLU, Sigmoid, GELU & Why
subsections.description: Without nonlinearity, your 100-layer network is a fancy matrix multiply. Activations are the gates that let neural networks think in curves.

subsections.title: Loss Functions: MSE, Cross-Entropy, Contrastive
subsections.description: Your network makes a prediction. The ground truth says otherwise. How wrong is it? That number is the loss. Pick the wrong loss function and your model optimizes for the wrong t…

subsections.title: Optimizers: SGD, Momentum, Adam, AdamW
subsections.description: Gradient descent tells you which direction to move. It says nothing about how far or how fast. SGD is a compass. Adam is GPS with traffic data.

subsections.title: Regularization: Dropout, Weight Decay, BatchNorm
subsections.description: Your model gets 99% on training data and 60% on test data. It memorized instead of learning. Regularization is the tax you impose on complexity to force generalization.

subsections.title: Weight Initialization & Training Stability
subsections.description: Initialize wrong and training never starts. Initialize right and 50 layers train as smoothly as 3.

subsections.title: Learning Rate Schedules & Warmup
subsections.description: The learning rate is the single most important hyperparameter. Not the architecture. Not the dataset size. Not the activation function. The learning rate. If you tune nothing el…

subsections.title: Build Your Own Mini Framework
subsections.description: You have built neurons, layers, networks, backprop, activations, loss functions, optimizers, regularization, initialization, and LR schedules. All as separate pieces. Now wire t…

subsections.title: Introduction to PyTorch
subsections.description: You built the engine from pistons and crankshafts. Now learn the one everyone actually drives.

subsections.title: Introduction to JAX
subsections.description: PyTorch mutates tensors. TensorFlow builds graphs. JAX compiles pure functions. That last one changes how you think about deep learning.

subsections.title: Debugging Neural Networks
subsections.description: Your network compiled. It ran. It produced a number. The number is wrong and nothing crashed. Welcome to the hardest kind of debugging -- the kind where there is no error message.

sections.title: Phase 04 · Computer Vision
sections.tagline: From pixels to understanding — image, video, 3D, VLMs, and world models.

subsections.title: Image Fundamentals: Pixels, Channels, Color Spaces
subsections.description: An image is a tensor of light samples. Every vision model you will ever use starts from this one fact.

subsections.title: Convolutions from Scratch
subsections.description: A convolution is a tiny dense layer you slide across an image, sharing the same weights at every location.

subsections.title: CNNs: LeNet to ResNet
subsections.description: Every major CNN of the last thirty years is the same conv–nonlinearity–downsample recipe with one new idea bolted on. Learn the ideas in order.

subsections.title: Image Classification
subsections.description: A classifier is a function from pixels to a probability distribution over classes. Everything else is plumbing.

subsections.title: Transfer Learning & Fine-Tuning
subsections.description: Somebody else spent a million GPU hours teaching a network what edges, textures, and object parts look like. You should borrow those features before training your own.

subsections.title: Object Detection — YOLO from Scratch
subsections.description: Detection is classification plus regression, run at every position in a feature map, then cleaned up with non-maximum suppression.

subsections.title: Semantic Segmentation — U-Net
subsections.description: Segmentation is classification at every pixel. U-Net makes it work by pairing a downsampling encoder with an upsampling decoder and wiring skip connections between them.

subsections.title: Instance Segmentation — Mask R-CNN
subsections.description: Add a tiny mask branch to a Faster R-CNN detector and you have instance segmentation. The hard part is RoIAlign, and it is harder than it looks.

subsections.title: Image Generation — GANs
subsections.description: A GAN is two neural networks in a fixed game. One draws, one critiques. They get better together until the drawings fool the critic.

subsections.title: Image Generation — Diffusion Models
subsections.description: A diffusion model learns to denoise. Train it to remove a tiny bit of noise from a noisy image, repeat that backwards a thousand times, and you have an image generator.

subsections.title: Stable Diffusion — Architecture & Fine-Tuning
subsections.description: Stable Diffusion is a DDPM that runs in the latent space of a pretrained VAE, conditioned on text via cross-attention, sampled with a fast deterministic ODE solver, and steered …

subsections.title: Video Understanding — Temporal Modeling
subsections.description: A video is a sequence of images plus the physics that connects them. Every video model either treats time as an extra axis (3D conv), a sequence to attend over (transformer), or…

subsections.title: 3D Vision: Point Clouds, NeRFs
subsections.description: 3D vision comes in two flavours. Point clouds are the sensor's raw output. NeRFs are the learned volumetric field. Both answer "what is where in space."

subsections.title: Vision Transformers (ViT)
subsections.description: Cut the image into patches, treat each patch as a word, run a standard transformer. Don't look back.

subsections.title: Real-Time Vision: Edge Deployment
subsections.description: Edge inference is the discipline of getting a 90%-accurate model to run at 30 fps on a device with 2 GB of RAM. Every percentage point of accuracy is traded against milliseconds…

subsections.title: Build a Complete Vision Pipeline
subsections.description: A production vision system is a chain of models and rules stitched with data contracts. The pieces are already in this phase; the capstone wires them together end-to-end.

subsections.title: Self-Supervised Vision — SimCLR, DINO, MAE
subsections.description: Labels are the bottleneck of supervised vision. Self-supervised pretraining removes them: learn visual features from 100M unlabelled images, fine-tune on 10k labelled ones.

subsections.title: Open-Vocabulary Vision — CLIP
subsections.description: Train an image encoder and a text encoder together so that matching (image, caption) pairs land at the same point in a shared space. That is the whole trick.

subsections.title: OCR & Document Understanding
subsections.description: OCR is a three-stage pipeline — detect text boxes, recognise the characters, then lay them out. Every modern OCR system reorders these stages or merges them.

subsections.title: Image Retrieval & Metric Learning
subsections.description: A retrieval system ranks candidates by a distance in embedding space. Metric learning is the discipline of shaping that space so the distances mean what you want.

subsections.title: Keypoint Detection & Pose Estimation
subsections.description: A pose is a set of ordered keypoints. A keypoint detector is a heatmap regressor. Everything else is bookkeeping.

subsections.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting from Scratch
subsections.description: A scene is a cloud of millions of 3D Gaussians. Each one has a position, orientation, scale, opacity, and a colour that depends on viewing direction. Rasterise them, backprop th…

subsections.title: Diffusion Transformers & Rectified Flow
subsections.description: The U-Net is not the secret of diffusion. Replace it with a transformer, swap the noise schedule for a straight-line flow, and suddenly you have SD3, FLUX, and every 2026 text-t…

subsections.title: SAM 3 & Open-Vocabulary Segmentation
subsections.description: Give a model a text prompt and an image and get masks for every matching object. SAM 3 made that a single forward pass.

subsections.title: Vision-Language Models (ViT-MLP-LLM)
subsections.description: A vision encoder converts an image into tokens. An MLP projector maps those tokens into the LLM's embedding space. A language model does the rest. That pattern — ViT-MLP-LLM — i…

subsections.title: Monocular Depth & Geometry Estimation
subsections.description: A depth map is a single-channel image where each pixel is a distance from the camera. Predicting it from one RGB frame used to be impossible without stereo or LiDAR. In 2026 a f…

subsections.title: Multi-Object Tracking & Video Memory
subsections.description: Tracking is detection plus association. Detect every frame. Match this frame's detections to last frame's tracks by ID.

subsections.title: World Models & Video Diffusion
subsections.description: A video model that predicts the next seconds of a scene is a world simulator. Condition that prediction on actions and you have a learned game engine.

sections.title: Phase 05 · NLP: Foundations to Advanced
sections.tagline: Language is the interface to intelligence.

subsections.title: Text Processing: Tokenization, Stemming, Lemmatization
subsections.description: Language is continuous. Models are discrete. Preprocessing is the bridge.

subsections.title: Bag of Words, TF-IDF & Text Representation
subsections.description: Count first, think later. TF-IDF still beats embeddings on well-defined tasks in 2026.

subsections.title: Word Embeddings: Word2Vec from Scratch
subsections.description: A word is the company it keeps. Train a shallow net on that idea and geometry falls out.

subsections.title: GloVe, FastText & Subword Embeddings
subsections.description: Word2Vec trained one embedding per word. GloVe factorized the co-occurrence matrix. FastText embedded the pieces. BPE bridged to transformers.

subsections.title: Sentiment Analysis
subsections.description: The canonical NLP task. Most of what you need to know about classical text classification shows up here.

subsections.title: Named Entity Recognition (NER)
subsections.description: Pull the names out. Sounds easy until you deal with ambiguous boundaries, nested entities, and domain jargon.

subsections.title: POS Tagging & Syntactic Parsing
subsections.description: Grammar was unfashionable for a while. Then every LLM pipeline needed to validate structured extraction, and it came back.

subsections.title: Text Classification — CNNs & RNNs for Text
subsections.description: Convolutions learn n-grams. Recurrences remember. Both are superseded by attention. Both still matter on constrained hardware.

subsections.title: Sequence-to-Sequence Models
subsections.description: Two RNNs pretending to be a translator. The bottleneck they hit is the reason attention exists.

subsections.title: Attention Mechanism — The Breakthrough
subsections.description: The decoder stops squinting at a compressed summary and starts looking at the whole source. Everything after this is attention plus engineering.

subsections.title: Machine Translation
subsections.description: Translation is the task that paid for NLP research for thirty years and keeps paying now.

subsections.title: Text Summarization
subsections.description: Extractive systems tell you what the document said. Abstractive systems tell you what the author meant. Different tasks, different pitfalls.

subsections.title: Question Answering Systems
subsections.description: Three systems shaped modern QA. Extractive found spans. Retrieval-augmented grounded them in documents. Generative produced answers. Every modern AI assistant is a mix of the th…

subsections.title: Information Retrieval & Search
subsections.description: BM25 is precise but brittle. Dense casts a wide net but misses keywords. Hybrid is the 2026 default. Everything else is tuning.

subsections.title: Topic Modeling: LDA, BERTopic
subsections.description: LDA: documents are mixtures of topics, topics are distributions over words. BERTopic: documents cluster in embedding space, clusters are topics. Same goal, different decompositi…

subsections.title: Text Generation
subsections.description: If a word is surprising, the model is bad. Perplexity makes surprise a number. Smoothing keeps it finite.

subsections.title: Chatbots: Rule-Based to Neural
subsections.description: ELIZA replied with pattern matches. DialogFlow mapped intents. GPT answered from weights. Claude runs tools and verifies. Each era solved the previous one's worst failure.

subsections.title: Multilingual NLP
subsections.description: One model, 100+ languages, zero training data for most of them. Cross-lingual transfer is the practical miracle of the 2020s.

subsections.title: Subword Tokenization: BPE, WordPiece, Unigram, SentencePiece
subsections.description: Word tokenizers choke on unseen words. Character tokenizers blow up sequence length. Subword tokenizers split the difference. Every modern LLM ships on one.

subsections.title: Structured Outputs & Constrained Decoding
subsections.description: Ask an LLM for JSON. Get JSON most of the time. In production, "most" is the problem. Constrained decoding turns "most" into "always" by editing the logits before sampling.

subsections.title: NLI & Textual Entailment

subsections.title: Diagram Reading Companion
subsections.description: Help an educator turn an authored SVG diagram and an explicit node-edge manifest into a keyboard-navigable explanation. Check that referenced nodes exist, expose branches and cycles, let the author review the reading order, and export an accessible HTML walkthrough plus graph JSON.

subsections.title: Distributed Eval Farm Coordinator
subsections.description: Build a persistent same-host evaluation coordinator that partitions recorded predictions, leases shards to real worker processes, fences stale completions and retains dataset-bound receipts.

subsections.title: Document QA With Citations and LangChain
subsections.description: A citation receipt that separates exact source support from relevance to the question. Import query(directory, question, model). A model callback returns JSON {source:chunk_id,quote:exact_text}. --response accepts a recorded response and applies the same gate.

subsections.title: Document Extraction Review Desk
subsections.description: Extract structured fields from a text document, inspect exact source spans, and approve ambiguous values before export.

subsections.title: Download Folder Sort Desk
subsections.description: Help someone organize local downloads by combining file metadata, content hashes and an explainable category score. Generate collision-free destination proposals and duplicate groups, then export an HTML review desk and a JSON move plan that another file manager can consume.

subsections.title: Durable Agent Jobs
subsections.description: Build a persistent local report queue with versioned leases, immutable input, idempotent output receipts and reproducible worker-process crash recovery.

subsections.title: Feedback Theme Board
subsections.description: Group product feedback with inspectable phrase evidence, count distinct sources, and export local issue drafts.

subsections.title: Field Notes Map Builder
subsections.description: Help a community mapping group explore observations supplied as coordinates, notes and optional photos. Validate locations, group nearby records using an explicit distance rule, preserve original observations during review, and export GeoJSON with a standalone map and observation table.

subsections.title: Glossary Hovercard Publisher
subsections.description: Help an educator add contextual definitions to existing lesson HTML using a reviewed glossary and longest-phrase matching. Preserve code and links, support keyboard-accessible definitions, and export a standalone annotated lesson with a reusable glossary file.

subsections.title: Harness Bench
subsections.description: Compare baseline, error-retry and evidence policies against the same ordered cases and model configuration. Count actual calls, reject incomparable receipts, replay finite recordings or call a configured HTTP model.

subsections.title: Hedged Request Lab
subsections.description: Help client developers evaluate delayed duplicate requests for safe reads. Send a second attempt only after a configurable delay, accept the first valid response, and record cancellation, late completion and duplicate service work separately. Export a bounded HTTP client and a latency-versus-work report from controlled local endpoints.

subsections.title: Inbox Triage Desk
subsections.description: Turn exported email into an evidence-backed review queue and unsent reply drafts.

subsections.title: Infrastructure Plan Explainer
subsections.description: Read a saved Terraform plan JSON for a developer reviewing a proposed change. Preserve unknown and sensitive-value markers, separate replacement from in-place updates, and trace declared dependencies. Produce a review brief whose explanations link to exact plan addresses; never apply the plan.

subsections.title: JSON Schema Output Guard
subsections.description: A schema preflight and bounded-repair receipt for model output contracts. Call guard(raw,schema) at the application boundary, or repair(generate,schema,maxAttempts) where generate receives structured Issue[] and a one-based attempt number.

subsections.title: Kubernetes Event Storyboard
subsections.description: Help an on-call engineer inspect exported Kubernetes events and workload snapshots. Group repeated events, distinguish observation time from occurrence time, and link each suggested investigation to object identity and rollout revision. Export an HTML timeline and a redacted JSON context pack for an assistant.

subsections.title: LLM Gateway With Fallbacks
subsections.description: Build a local non-streaming HTTP proxy with real provider fallback, per-provider environment credentials, response limits, and one overall deadline. Verify the complete wire path with loopback servers.

subsections.title: Local Model Evaluation Harness
subsections.description: A reproducible local-model recording and comparison artifact with visible coverage and confidence error. record.py writes the same {manifest,source,labels,records} contract consumed by cli.py. --baseline compares only identical label fingerprints; --min-accuracy supplies a local CI gate.

subsections.title: Log Volume Reduction Lab
subsections.description: Help an engineer build compact log context for an assistant. Learn bounded template grouping, counts and representative examples, then compare uniform and rarity-aware sampling on authored failure fixtures. Export compressed JSONL and a coverage report showing which important events were lost.

subsections.title: MCP Tool Discovery Workbench
subsections.description: A scoped MCP inventory server that discovers schemas inside a measured context budget. Run python3 cli.py /absolute/inventory.json --serve as a stdio server. tools/call catalog_search takes query, max_chars and k; the response returns selected public schemas and their character count.

subsections.title: Meeting Notes to Actions
subsections.description: A source-linked commitment inbox whose export requires an explicit review decision. Use the schema_version1 actions.json receipt with stable action ids and original source lines. CSV columns are id, owner, due and task, and contain approved actions only.

subsections.title: Persistent Memory Server
subsections.description: A persistent memory workbench with revision history and one boundary for REST and MCP. Set MEMORY_TOKEN in the environment and run node cli.ts --data-dir memory-data --serve --port 8788. REST and MCP share the same store; no token is written into files.

subsections.title: Mini Decompiler
subsections.description: A decompiler for a defined x86-64 subset that turns functions in an ELF relocatable object you compiled into structured C. It recompiles its own output, runs a differential test over an input grid, compares relocation-masked bytes and writes an evidence report that lists every unknown.

subsections.title: Multi-Agent Code Review Panel
subsections.description: A review disagreement workbench that measures when quorum helps and when it hides findings. Input files maps names to text or lines. Optional reviewers contain id,cost,findings recordings. Expected labels use {file,line,rule}; the report records the source fingerprint and per-reviewer versus consensus metrics.

subsections.title: Plain Language Rewrite Desk
subsections.description: Help a technical author revise dense prose using visible sentence and vocabulary measures, protected terms and an optional real rewriting provider. Compare original and proposed paragraphs, surface changed numbers and missing definitions, and export only the author's accepted revisions with a Markdown change record.

subsections.title: Incident Postmortem Writer
subsections.description: Turn your JSONL incident logs and review decisions into an HTML evidence desk, exact-quote checks, owned actions and a source-bound approval receipt.

subsections.title: PR Review Reporter
subsections.description: A local patch-review artifact that preserves Git line evidence and can enter CI as SARIF. Use --diff - for stdin, --repo /path --base REF --head REF for a read-only Git diff, or --candidates recorded-findings.json to validate another reviewer's findings against the supplied patch.

subsections.title: Prompt Regression Tester
subsections.description: Compare prompt revisions on recorded responses with explicit checks, paired regressions, and a reproducible release gate.

subsections.title: RAG Freshness Pipeline
subsections.description: Build a content-addressed document index with deletion tracking, version checks, and freshness-aware retrieval.

subsections.title: Report Judge
subsections.description: Audit sentence-level citations, test lexical support, and compare report revisions with a paired uncertainty interval.

subsections.title: Research Report Agent
subsections.description: Build the pipeline behind deep research tools: search a corpus, pull exact snippets, plan the research, write only from evidence, verify every claim, publish an HTML report with footnotes and a trace, then score it on checked-in public evaluation fixtures.

subsections.title: Retrieval Evaluation Lab
subsections.description: Measure ranking quality with precision, recall, reciprocal rank, and discounted gain while exposing duplicates and missing judgments.

subsections.title: Retry Storm Lab
subsections.description: Help SDK authors choose retry behavior when many clients fail together. Replay concurrent clients against a deterministic service model, compare bounded backoff and jitter with a shared retry budget, then run the same policy against a local HTTP fixture. Export amplification and recovery timelines with a reusable client policy.

subsections.title: Streaming Agent Shell in Rust
subsections.description: Build a real stdin/stdout Rust action loop with bounded reads, an explicit command grammar, path containment, and streamed JSON events.

subsections.title: Sandbox Policy Planner
subsections.description: Select a modeled isolation policy, inspect an optional local Docker invocation, and compare requested controls with observed harmless probes.

subsections.title: Self-Improving Skill Loop
subsections.description: Improve an explicit routing skill from labeled development errors, then require a separate evaluation gate before promotion.

subsections.title: Semantic Notes Search
subsections.description: Search local notes with explicit synonym expansion and normalized TF-IDF scores. Explain every match rather than hiding retrieval in a hosted embedding service.

subsections.title: Sensitive Text Redaction Gate
subsections.description: Detect ASCII email patterns, valid IPv4 addresses and explicit literal identifiers. Merge overlapping spans, replace their union without exposing original values in receipts, and export redacted JSONL plus an inspectable HTML ledger.

subsections.title: Service Ownership Navigator
subsections.description: Combine an authored service catalog, repository ownership rules and runbook links into a local directory. Resolve ownership at the requested path, surface conflicts and missing runbooks, and answer handoff questions with file-level evidence. Export a static site and JSON lookup interface without sending notifications.

subsections.title: Signed Webhook Inbox
subsections.description: Help developers feed external events into an agent workflow without losing retries or accepting altered payloads. Verify an authored signature scheme over the raw body, enforce timestamp bounds, and store stable delivery identities before dispatch. Export an HTTP receiver and a replay CLI that distinguishes a transport retry from a new business event.

subsections.title: Cross-Agent Skill Installer
subsections.description: Validate local skill bundles, translate agent metadata, verify content digests, and atomically install without overwriting learner edits.

subsections.title: Skill Router
subsections.description: Route a request to a skill using explainable keyword scores, path rules, permission gates, and dependency ordering.

subsections.title: Skill Supply-Chain Scanner
subsections.description: Build an offline advisory scanner that preserves UTF-8 offsets, reports explicit policy patterns, scores distinct findings and emits a review gate. It is a transparent heuristic, not a malware detector or a promise that unflagged skills are safe.

subsections.title: SKILL.md Validator and Loader
subsections.description: Build a bounded Agent Skills loader with a deliberately small frontmatter grammar, strict metadata validation, safe reference paths, and progressive disclosure. The supported YAML subset is explicit; unsupported forms fail instead of being guessed.

subsections.title: Source-Grounded Study Coach
subsections.description: Build practice questions with source evidence and a visible review schedule.

subsections.title: Streaming Answer Recovery
subsections.description: Build a browser answer view and local event stream for developers integrating assistant output. Handle split UTF-8 bytes, event IDs, reconnection, cancellation and partial citations. Preserve the difference between an interrupted draft and a completed answer, with a downloadable event trace to reproduce rendering failures.

subsections.title: Subtitle Localization Desk
subsections.description: Help a course creator localize supplied WebVTT captions through a glossary, an optional real translation provider and an explicit review step. Preserve cue identities and timestamps, flag text that exceeds the chosen reading budget, and export reviewed captions with a side-by-side HTML desk.

subsections.title: Support Agent With Google ADK
subsections.description: Build a redacted, authorized support review with retained replies and evidence, then run the same policy through real Google ADK agents.

subsections.title: Tiny Coding Agent
subsections.description: Build a bounded coding loop that applies exact patches to a disposable workspace and runs its real tests through an allowlisted tool contract.

subsections.title: Token Counter and Cost Meter
subsections.description: Build an explicit approximate tokenizer, exact recorded-usage accounting, rate-card cost calculation and budget admission. Estimates are labeled and never presented as provider tokenizer counts. Prices are fixture inputs rather than claims about current provider pricing.

subsections.title: Tool Call Firewall
subsections.description: Build a deny-by-default policy evaluator with bounded arguments, role permissions, single-use approvals and a structured audit log. The artifact is a library gate; applications must place it before every real tool execution.

subsections.title: Typed Workflow Agent with Mastra
subsections.description: Build a typed approval workflow, then preserve and resume real Mastra suspension through a local SQLite store.

subsections.title: UI String Localization Workbench
subsections.description: Help a small product team localize JSON message catalogs while retaining stable keys, variable placeholders and contextual notes. Compare recorded or real provider proposals in a UI preview, require review of ambiguous strings, and export an approved locale catalog and unresolved-string queue.

subsections.title: Visual Evidence Library
subsections.description: Find text inside screenshots and diagrams with inspectable coordinate evidence.

subsections.title: Vocabulary Autocomplete Pad
subsections.description: Help a writer reuse their own terminology with a small local autocomplete model built from token counts, prefixes and short word histories. Show the evidence behind each suggestion and export an interactive writing pad plus a portable vocabulary model for another editor.

subsections.title: Voice Note Transcriber Pipeline
subsections.description: Turn a selected WAV into an inspectable transcript and caption review page using a real optional HTTP recognizer, with an honest offline speech fixture.

subsections.title: Web Change Brief
subsections.description: Turn noisy HTML snapshots into a small report of exact readable text changes.

subsections.title: Self-Correcting Workflow Hooks
subsections.description: Turn repeated, sourced corrections into scoped rules, persist them atomically, and enforce only explicitly approved rules.

subsections.title: Workshop Materials Planner
subsections.description: Help a workshop host reconcile per-participant materials, reusable equipment and an inventory snapshot. Use explicit unit conversions and declared sharing rules to compute shortages, keep unconvertible quantities visible, and export a packing list with a participant-count comparison.

sections.title: Planned projects
sections.tagline: Upstream plans are preserved as plans; they do not have completed implementations.

subsections.title: Photo Burst Contact Sheet
subsections.description: Help a creator review repeated shots by computing simple pixel fingerprints and an inspectable sharpness measure. Group candidate duplicates, preserve the photographer's final choice, and export a contact sheet plus a selection manifest for an editor.

subsections.title: Dependency Upgrade Impact Map
subsections.description: Help a maintainer review an upgrade using supplied before/after API signatures and a bounded source parser. Map changed symbols to actual call sites, distinguish confirmed incompatibilities from unresolved uses, and emit a targeted test checklist. An optional model can explain evidence but cannot invent removed APIs.

subsections.title: Gesture Shortcut Pad
subsections.description: Help a presenter or educator control a local practice application with a few self-recorded gestures. Normalize pointer strokes, compare them with an explicit sequence-distance algorithm, expose uncertain matches, and export a portable gesture profile plus a small browser integration demo.

subsections.title: CI Failure Reproducer
subsections.description: Help a contributor reproduce a failed job from an exported workflow log, commit identity and declared environment. Identify the first failing command, distinguish infrastructure failures from test failures, and produce an allowlisted local replay recipe. Retain the original log lines beside every generated instruction.

subsections.title: Label Adjudication Desk
subsections.description: Help a small team create useful evaluation labels without silently replacing disagreement with majority vote. Import independently labeled records, blind annotator identities during review, group disagreements and capture an explicit final decision with its evidence. Export a local review page and versioned JSONL that preserves both original labels and adjudication history.

subsections.title: Lost Item Match Desk
subsections.description: Help a community venue match lost-item descriptions with photographed found objects. Combine explicit text features, simple image-color descriptors and optional reviewed vision proposals, then export an HTML candidate-pair desk and a decision file for the venue's existing records.

subsections.title: Presentation Rehearsal Coach
subsections.description: Help a speaker improve a rehearsal by aligning supplied slide text and timed transcript segments. Compute explicit pacing and topic-coverage signals, show the source phrases behind suggested practice targets, and export a slide-by-slide HTML report with a reusable rehearsal comparison file.

subsections.title: Semantic Cache Correctness Lab
subsections.description: Build an opt-in answer cache that binds entries to tenant, model, source revision and expiry. Compare exact and semantic candidate matching using authored near-miss questions, including changed numbers and negation. Export a local HTTP adapter and a false-hit report; similarity alone must not authorize cross-user reuse.

subsections.title: Tool Contract Migration Checker
subsections.description: Help tool authors evolve a callable interface while existing agents still hold old argument shapes. Compare a documented subset of before-and-after schemas, generate counterexamples for required fields and narrowed values, and replay saved calls through both validators. Export a compatibility report and reviewable migration fixtures for CI.

subsections.title: Video Highlight Storyboard
subsections.description: Help a tutorial creator assemble short excerpts from a supplied video, frame samples and timed transcript. Combine visible shot changes with transcript topic scores, preserve exact source time ranges, and export a playable storyboard and edit-decision JSON for a video editor.

subsections.title: A2A Task Handoff Workbench
subsections.description: Help teams connect agents that expose different capabilities and task lifecycles. Read Agent Cards, choose a mutually supported binding, and run a handoff that includes a request for more input, cancellation and a final artifact. Export a local client-server pair and a replayable receipt showing every state transition and artifact owner.

subsections.title: Abstention Calibration Workbench
subsections.description: Help teams set a defensible accept-or-defer rule for a bounded task. Tune a score threshold on labeled development records under explicit error costs, freeze that policy, and evaluate held-out risk and coverage across slices. Export a decision-policy file and audit that shows how many requests need human review.

subsections.title: Artifact Provenance Gate
subsections.description: Help a maintainer inspect a downloaded agent plugin or release artifact before integrating it. Verify the subject digest and attestation signature, evaluate declared builder and source identities against an explicit policy, and preserve the reason for every rejection. Export a CI gate with authored signed fixtures and a separately verified external-verifier adapter.

subsections.title: Context Compaction Verifier
subsections.description: Help agent developers avoid losing a user constraint during a long session. Track explicit facts and constraints with source locators, create an extractive compressed context, and test candidate summaries against a declared retention contract. Export compaction middleware that keeps the prior snapshot when required evidence disappears.

subsections.title: Local Inference Capacity Planner
subsections.description: Help a team choose a concurrency limit for its own model endpoint. Replay an authored arrival schedule, record queue wait separately from service time, and compare observed percentiles and timeouts across bounded runs. Export a capacity curve and editable operating limit based on measured requests, not model-name lookup tables.

subsections.title: MCP Compatibility Doctor
subsections.description: Help an integration author diagnose a client that connects but cannot use a server correctly. Run authored negotiation, request-correlation and capability probes through a bounded transport adapter. Export a compatibility matrix and the smallest wire transcript that explains a failure, with credentials removed.

subsections.title: Metamorphic Evaluation Workbench
subsections.description: Help evaluators catch inconsistent behavior across related inputs. Author transformations such as unit conversion, record reordering and equivalent formatting, define the output relationship each should preserve, and shrink violating examples. Export a property-based evaluation runner and small failure bundles that can be consumed by CI.

subsections.title: OAuth Resource Boundary Lab
subsections.description: Help developers integrate delegated authorization without accepting a token intended for another service. Build local authorization and resource fixtures, follow metadata discovery, bind authorization to the requested resource, and check audience and scope at the server. Export reusable validation middleware and a redacted explanation of rejected requests.

subsections.title: Outbound Request Policy Proxy
subsections.description: Help developers constrain a fetch tool that follows URLs supplied by untrusted documents. Evaluate the scheme, host, resolved address and each redirect, then connect using the validated destination under explicit size and time limits. Export a local egress adapter and loopback cases that reveal redirect and address-policy mistakes.

subsections.title: Release Canary Decision Lab
subsections.description: Help a team decide whether an agent behavior change is ready for wider exposure. Assign stable request cohorts, compare candidate and baseline error and latency windows, and distinguish insufficient evidence from a failed gate. Export replayable decision receipts and a local shadow adapter that exercises the policy without deploying anything.

subsections.title: Secret Injection Sidecar
subsections.description: Help developers keep service credentials out of model-visible tool arguments and routine traces. Build a local broker that resolves opaque handles, binds each handle to a destination and operation, and inserts environment-supplied credentials at the network boundary. Test echoed credential markers and export decision receipts with bounded response filtering.

subsections.title: Tenant Fairness Scheduler
subsections.description: Help platform developers share a finite worker pool across tenants with different job sizes. Implement weighted deficit scheduling, bounded admission and aging, then compare per-tenant wait distributions under authored bursts. Export a queue adapter and workload receipts that make starvation and unused capacity visible.

subsections.title: Agent Resource Deadlock Lab
subsections.description: Help developers coordinate agents that need several exclusive resources, such as a browser session and a workspace. Build wait-for graphs, explore bounded schedules, and compare ordered acquisition with timeout-and-release policies. Export deadlock traces and a resource-coordinator adapter with explicit acquisition receipts.

subsections.title: Judge Bias Calibration Lab
subsections.description: Help evaluators decide whether an automated pairwise judge is useful for their task. Blind candidate identities, swap answer positions, run authored length counterfactuals and compare decisions with held-out human anchors. Export disagreement and bias breakdowns plus a versioned rubric and judge configuration receipt.

subsections.title: Trajectory Counterexample Minimizer
subsections.description: Help agent developers diagnose failures that depend on action order. Express bounded temporal rules such as approval preceding an effect, check event traces, and remove irrelevant events while preserving declared causal dependencies. Export a minimal replay bundle with the violated rule and exact event identities.

subsections.title: Transactional Workspace Patch Broker
subsections.description: Help concurrent coding agents avoid overwriting each other's files halfway through a multi-file change. Bind a patch bundle to content hashes, apply it to a private versioned workspace, run declared checks, and publish by switching one workspace pointer. Export a transaction API with conflict evidence and an explicit rollback journal.
