Agent Skills Engineering
subsections.description: Build, route, secure, evaluate, package, and verify Agent Skills in real hosts.

subsections.title: Agent Systems Engineering
subsections.description: Engineer tool-using agent loops with explicit context, memory, orchestration, safety, evaluation, and production control.

subsections.title: AI Data Systems
subsections.description: Build reliable data, feature, embedding, retrieval, evaluation, and observability pipelines for AI systems.

subsections.title: Developer Experience and Education
subsections.description: Build credible integrations, examples, and reusable agent packages, then turn developer friction into clearer tools and teaching.

subsections.title: AI Evaluation and Reliability
subsections.description: Measure model and agent behavior, expose failure modes, instrument the runtime, and build release and incident controls around evidence.

subsections.title: LLM Product Engineering
subsections.description: Turn language-model capability into evaluated, safe, cost-aware product behavior that can survive production traffic.

subsections.title: Building and Deploying AI Applications
subsections.description: Build an AI feature from prompt and structured output through retrieval, evaluation, production serving, observability, and release.

subsections.title: Customer AI Deployment
subsections.description: Discover a customer workflow, reduce its riskiest assumptions, and carry a useful AI system through measurement and rollout.

subsections.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
subsections.description: Build, secure, verify, and operate stateless MCP systems from JSON-RPC envelopes through conformance release gates.

subsections.title: Reverse Engineering
subsections.description: Read a compiled program you built yourself: parse the file, decode the instructions, lift them to pseudocode, record evidence, and prove a rebuild equal, then learn the field around that pipeline with its main tools.

subsections.title: Product Judgment and Delivery
subsections.description: Turn evidence into outcomes, assumptions, testable slices, executable specifications, measurement plans, and owned feedback loops.

subsections.title: Software Engineering Fundamentals
subsections.description: Build the repository, debugging, testing, interface, security, release, and operational foundations AI systems depend on.

subsections.title: Agent-Assisted Engineering
subsections.description: Frame, plan, execute, delegate, verify, review, and improve coding-agent work inside real repositories.

subsections.title: Activation Checkpointing
subsections.description: A training-memory technique that saves only selected forward-pass activations and recomputes the omitted ones during backpropagation.

subsections.title: Activation Function
subsections.description: A function applied after a linear or affine layer that introduces nonlinearity. Without it, composing layers with weights and biases collapses to one affine transformation. ReLU, GELU, and SiLU are common choices. The choice directly affects whether gradients flow during training.

subsections.title: Adam (Optimizer)
subsections.description: Adaptive Moment Estimation. It combines an exponential average of gradients with an exponential average of squared gradients, applies bias correction, and adapts the update scale per parameter. It is a useful baseline, but it still needs a suitable learning rate and schedule.

subsections.title: AdamW
subsections.description: An Adam variant that decouples weight decay from the gradient-based parameter update. That makes the shrinkage behavior easier to reason about than adding an L2 penalty inside Adam's adaptively scaled gradient.

subsections.title: Admission Control
subsections.description: A pre-acceptance gate that decides whether a request may enter a bounded queue or service under the system's current capacity, priority, and policy.

subsections.title: Agent
subsections.description: A software system that lets a model select actions toward a goal, observe tool or environment results, and continue under an orchestration policy. An agent may use a loop, a state machine, a workflow engine, or human approvals. The model is one component, not the entire system.

subsections.title: Agent Harness
subsections.description: The runtime around a model that assembles context, exposes tools, manages state, enforces limits, records traces, and decides when the agent should continue, retry, ask, or stop.

subsections.title: Agent Memory
subsections.description: Information stored outside the model and selected for use in later agent steps, such as prior decisions, user preferences, task episodes, or verified facts.

subsections.title: Agent State
subsections.description: The explicit data an agent carries across steps, such as the current objective, completed actions, tool results, open questions, budgets, approvals, and artifact references.

subsections.title: Agent Skill
subsections.description: A discoverable directory of procedural instructions whose entry point is `SKILL.md`, with optional references, scripts, and assets that a compatible runtime can load in stages.

subsections.title: AI Risk Assessment
subsections.description: A documented analysis of how an AI system can affect people, organizations, and environments, including context, hazards, likelihood, impact, controls, residual risk, and monitoring responsibilities.

subsections.title: Alignment
subsections.description: The effort to make a model or AI system behave in ways that match intended goals, constraints, and human preferences across both expected and adversarial situations.

subsections.title: Approval Gate
subsections.description: A control point that blocks a consequential action until an authorized person or policy grants permission.

subsections.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN)
subsections.description: A search method that returns vectors likely to be among the nearest to a query without exhaustively comparing the query with every stored vector.

subsections.title: Attention
subsections.description: A mechanism that forms contextual representations by comparing query vectors with key vectors, normalizing the resulting scores, and using them to combine value vectors. Masks, position rules, or sparse patterns can restrict which positions participate.

subsections.title: Audio Token
subsections.description: A discrete identifier produced by an audio codec or tokenizer for a short segment or feature of an audio signal, sometimes across several codebooks.

subsections.title: Audit Log
subsections.description: A durable, access-controlled record of security- or accountability-relevant events, including who or what acted, what changed, when it happened, and the resulting status.

subsections.title: Autograd
subsections.description: A system that records or transforms tensor operations so it can compute derivatives, usually with reverse-mode automatic differentiation. You write the forward computation and the framework derives the gradients needed for backpropagation.

subsections.title: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)
subsections.description: The task and system pipeline that maps a speech signal to a transcription, often with optional token or segment timing and confidence information.

subsections.title: Autoregressive
subsections.description: A factorization in which each output token is predicted from the tokens that precede it. During generation, the selected token is appended to the sequence and becomes part of the next prediction's context.

subsections.title: Autoscaling
subsections.description: A control loop that changes the number or capacity of serving workers from observed demand, resource use, or application metrics within configured bounds.

subsections.title: Availability
subsections.description: The proportion of eligible service interactions or time windows in which users can obtain the defined acceptable service under a stated measurement boundary.

subsections.title: Backpressure
subsections.description: A flow-control mechanism that slows or rejects upstream work when a downstream component cannot process it safely at the current rate.

subsections.title: Backpropagation
subsections.description: An efficient application of the chain rule that propagates derivatives from a scalar loss backward through a computation graph. It computes gradients; an optimizer uses those gradients to update parameters.

subsections.title: Batch Size
subsections.description: The number of examples whose losses contribute to one gradient estimate before an optimizer update. Larger batches can improve hardware utilization and reduce gradient noise, but they require more memory and may need different learning-rate or scheduling choices.

subsections.title: Benchmark Contamination
subsections.description: Overlap or information leakage between evaluation examples and data used to pretrain, tune, prompt, select, or otherwise improve the evaluated system.

subsections.title: BM25
subsections.description: A lexical ranking function that scores a document from query-term matches while accounting for term rarity, repeated occurrences, and document length.

subsections.title: Byte Pair Encoding (BPE)
subsections.description: A subword-tokenization method that repeatedly merges frequent adjacent units to construct a fixed vocabulary from training text.

subsections.title: Calibration
subsections.description: The agreement between a system's stated confidence and the observed frequency with which predictions at that confidence are correct.

subsections.title: Canary Release
subsections.description: A deployment strategy that exposes a new version to a limited slice of traffic or infrastructure before expanding the rollout.

subsections.title: Chain of Thought (CoT)
subsections.description: Intermediate reasoning used to decompose a task before producing an answer. A prompt can request a visible rationale, while some systems use internal reasoning that is not returned to the user.

subsections.title: Checkpoint
subsections.description: A durable snapshot used to resume from a known boundary. In a workflow, it stores operational state and artifact references. In model training, it can store parameters, optimizer state, scheduler state, and the training position.

subsections.title: Chunked Prefill
subsections.description: A serving technique that divides a long prompt's prefill work into smaller schedulable pieces so prompt processing can interleave with decode work from other requests.

subsections.title: Chunking
subsections.description: Dividing source material into retrievable units before indexing. Chunk boundaries, overlap, metadata, and document structure determine whether retrieval returns enough context without flooding the prompt.

subsections.title: Circuit Breaker
subsections.description: A reliability control that temporarily stops calls to a dependency after failures cross a threshold, then probes whether the dependency has recovered.

subsections.title: CNN (Convolutional Neural Network)
subsections.description: A neural network that uses convolution operations (sliding filters over the input) to detect local patterns. Stacking convolutions detects increasingly complex features: edges, textures, objects.

subsections.title: Coding Agent
subsections.description: An agent specialized for software work that can inspect a repository, edit files, run development tools, and use their outputs to advance a scoped engineering task.

subsections.title: Compensating Action
subsections.description: A deliberate operation that semantically counteracts a completed side effect when the original operation cannot be rolled back atomically.

subsections.title: Content Provenance
subsections.description: Verifiable information about the origin and editing history of a piece of media or other digital content, including the actors, tools, transformations, and assertions attached to it.

subsections.title: Context Compression
subsections.description: Reducing the token footprint of source material while attempting to preserve the information required for a later model decision.

subsections.title: Context Engineering
subsections.description: Designing the full information environment supplied to a model at each step, including instructions, selected files, retrieved evidence, tool results, examples, state, and output constraints.

subsections.title: Context Window
subsections.description: The maximum token capacity available to one model inference under a specific model and API contract. The capacity may include system instructions, messages, retrieved content, tool exchanges, and generated output, with provider-specific accounting and output limits.

subsections.title: Continuous Batching
subsections.description: A serving scheduler that adds and removes generation requests at iteration boundaries instead of waiting for every request in a fixed batch to finish.

subsections.title: Contrastive Learning
subsections.description: Training by pulling similar pairs closer and pushing dissimilar pairs apart in embedding space. CLIP uses this: matching image-text pairs vs non-matching ones.

subsections.title: Cosine Similarity
subsections.description: The normalized dot product of two vectors. It compares their direction rather than their magnitude and ranges from -1 to 1 for real-valued vectors.

subsections.title: Cost per Successful Task
subsections.description: Total system cost divided by the number of tasks that satisfy a defined success criterion, including retries, failed runs, tool use, and evaluation overhead.

subsections.title: Cross-Attention
subsections.description: Attention in which the query representation comes from one sequence or representation while keys and values come from another.

subsections.title: Cross-Entropy
subsections.description: A loss based on the negative log probability assigned to the target outcome. In next-token training, it penalizes the model when it assigns low probability to the observed next token.

subsections.title: CUDA
subsections.description: NVIDIA's platform and programming model for general-purpose computation on compatible GPUs. Deep-learning frameworks use CUDA libraries and kernels to execute many tensor operations in parallel.

subsections.title: Data Augmentation
subsections.description: Creating modified examples, such as transformed images, perturbed audio, or paraphrased text, to increase training diversity without collecting entirely new source data. It can reduce overfitting when the transformation preserves the task signal.

subsections.title: Data Classification
subsections.description: Assigning data to documented sensitivity or impact classes so handling, access, retention, sharing, and incident rules follow the consequences of disclosure or loss.

subsections.title: Data Deduplication
subsections.description: Detecting and removing exact and near-duplicate examples within or across datasets.

subsections.title: Data Exfiltration
subsections.description: Unauthorized transfer of protected data from a system or trust zone to a person, tool, service, or storage location that is not permitted to receive it.

subsections.title: Data Leakage
subsections.description: Unintended use of information during training or feature construction that would not be available at the real prediction point or belongs to a held-out evaluation boundary.

subsections.title: Data Lineage
subsections.description: A record of how a data artifact was derived across sources, transformations, joins, filters, versions, and downstream uses.

subsections.title: Data Minimization
subsections.description: For personal data, limiting what is collected, processed, exposed, and retained to what is necessary for a specified purpose. Teams can apply the same discipline to sensitive non-personal data as an engineering control.

subsections.title: Data Provenance
subsections.description: Traceable information about where data originated, who or what transformed it, which versions were used, and how derived artifacts relate to their sources.

subsections.title: Dataset Split
subsections.description: A documented partition of examples into separate subsets for fitting, development decisions, and final evaluation.

subsections.title: Datasheet for Datasets
subsections.description: Structured documentation of a dataset's motivation, composition, collection process, preprocessing, uses, distribution, maintenance, and known limitations.

subsections.title: Deadline Propagation
subsections.description: Passing the remaining end-to-end time budget to downstream calls so each dependency knows how long the original request can still usefully wait.

subsections.title: Decode Phase
subsections.description: The iterative stage of autoregressive inference that generates new tokens one step at a time after the input prefix has been processed.

subsections.title: Decoder
subsections.description: A component that maps a representation into an output. In an encoder-decoder transformer, the decoder uses masked self-attention and cross-attention to generate outputs. Decoder-only language models instead generate from a single causal stack.

subsections.title: Decoding Strategy
subsections.description: The algorithm that converts a model's sequence of next-token scores into selected tokens and a completed output.

subsections.title: Defense in Depth
subsections.description: Using independent preventive, detective, and corrective controls at several system boundaries so one failed control does not determine the outcome.

subsections.title: Delegation
subsections.description: Assigning a bounded subtask to another person or agent together with the needed context, authority, output contract, and return conditions.

subsections.title: Dense Retrieval
subsections.description: First-stage retrieval that embeds queries and candidates into vector representations and ranks candidates by a similarity function.

subsections.title: Diffusion Model
subsections.description: A generative model trained around a progressive noising process and a learned reverse process. Sampling usually begins from noise and applies repeated denoising steps, sometimes in a learned latent space.

subsections.title: Disaggregated Serving
subsections.description: A serving architecture that runs prefill and decode work in separately provisioned worker pools and transfers the required attention state between them.

subsections.title: Distribution Shift
subsections.description: A difference between the data distribution used to build or evaluate a system and the distribution it encounters after deployment.

subsections.title: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
subsections.description: A preference-optimization objective that trains a policy directly from preferred and rejected response pairs relative to a reference policy. It avoids running an explicit reward model and reinforcement-learning loop during this stage.

subsections.title: Dropout
subsections.description: During training, randomly setting a fraction of activations to zero encourages the network not to rely on one activation path. It is normally disabled for standard inference, although Monte Carlo dropout deliberately keeps it active to estimate uncertainty.

subsections.title: Durable Execution
subsections.description: Running a workflow so its state and completed steps survive process crashes, restarts, or long waits without redoing confirmed side effects.

subsections.title: Dynamic Batching
subsections.description: A runtime policy that forms inference batches from queued requests according to compatible shapes, maximum size, priority, and allowed queue delay.

subsections.title: Early Fusion
subsections.description: Combining raw or low-level representations from several modalities before most task-specific modeling occurs.

subsections.title: Eigenvalue
subsections.description: A scalar that describes how a linear transformation scales a corresponding nonzero eigenvector without changing its direction. In covariance-matrix PCA, larger eigenvalues correspond to directions with more variance.

subsections.title: Embedding
subsections.description: A learned mapping from discrete items (words, images, users) to dense vectors in continuous space, where similar items end up close together

subsections.title: Encoder
subsections.description: A component that transforms input into a representation. A transformer encoder commonly uses non-causal self-attention, subject to any masks, so each position can incorporate context from across the input.

subsections.title: Epoch
subsections.description: One traversal of the defined training dataset. In distributed or sampled training, the exact implementation of an epoch depends on the data loader and sampling policy.

subsections.title: Error Budget
subsections.description: The amount of unsuccessful service allowed by a service-level objective over its measurement window before the objective is exhausted.

subsections.title: Eval Set
subsections.description: A versioned collection of inputs, expected properties, scoring rules, and metadata used to measure an AI system against a defined capability or risk.

subsections.title: Evaluation (Eval)
subsections.description: A defined process for measuring model or system behavior on representative tasks using explicit success criteria, data, scorers, and review procedures.

subsections.title: Exact Match (EM)
subsections.description: A metric that counts an output as correct only when its normalized representation exactly equals an accepted reference answer.

subsections.title: Expert Parallelism
subsections.description: Distributing mixture-of-experts subnetworks across devices and routing each token's activations to the devices that host its selected experts.

subsections.title: Feature
subsections.description: An individual measurable property of the data. In classical ML, you engineer features by hand. In deep learning, the network learns features automatically from raw data.

subsections.title: Few-Shot
subsections.description: In-context learning that includes a small set of demonstrations before the target input so the model can infer the desired task, format, or decision boundary.

subsections.title: Fine-tuning
subsections.description: Continuing training from pretrained parameters on a narrower dataset or objective. Depending on the method, you may update all parameters, selected parameters, or added adapter parameters.

subsections.title: Flaky Test
subsections.description: A test that can pass and fail across equivalent runs without a relevant change to the code or intended test environment.

subsections.title: FlashAttention
subsections.description: An exact attention algorithm that tiles the computation to reduce transfers between accelerator memory levels while avoiding materialization of the full attention matrix in high-bandwidth memory.

subsections.title: Function Calling
subsections.description: A provider or application interface through which a model emits a structured request naming a tool and its arguments. Application code validates the request, performs the operation, and can return the result for another model step.

subsections.title: GAN (Generative Adversarial Network)
subsections.description: A generator network tries to create realistic data while a discriminator network tries to tell real from fake. They train together: the generator gets better at fooling the discriminator, and the discriminator gets better at detecting fakes.

subsections.title: Goodput
subsections.description: The rate of completed requests that satisfy defined service constraints, such as both time-to-first-token and per-token latency objectives, under a stated workload.

subsections.title: GPT
subsections.description: Generative Pre-trained Transformer, a family label for generative transformer models pretrained on sequence-prediction objectives and adapted for downstream use. Product names and model architectures should not be treated as interchangeable.

subsections.title: Graceful Degradation
subsections.description: Preserving a bounded core service when capacity or dependencies are impaired by reducing optional quality, features, freshness, or workload instead of failing every request.

subsections.title: Gradient
subsections.description: A vector of partial derivatives pointing in the direction of steepest increase. In ML, you go opposite to the gradient (gradient descent) to minimize the loss.

subsections.title: Gradient Accumulation
subsections.description: Summing or averaging gradients from several microbatches before performing one optimizer update.

subsections.title: Gradient Clipping
subsections.description: Limiting gradient values or their combined norm before an optimizer update when they exceed a chosen threshold.

subsections.title: Gradient Descent
subsections.description: A family of optimization updates that move parameters using the negative gradient of an objective, usually estimated from batches rather than the entire dataset.

subsections.title: Grounding
subsections.description: Connecting a generated answer or action to evidence, state, or observations that the system can identify and check.

subsections.title: Guardrails
subsections.description: System controls that constrain inputs, tool use, outputs, permissions, and escalation. They can include schemas, policy checks, classifiers, allowlists, sandboxing, approvals, and post-action verification.

subsections.title: Hallucination
subsections.description: Generated content that is false, unsupported by the available evidence, or inconsistent with the task's source of truth. It can arise even when the output is fluent and the model is not attempting to deceive.

subsections.title: Handoff
subsections.description: A structured transfer of a task between people or agents that preserves the objective, current state, evidence, decisions, constraints, and remaining work.

subsections.title: HNSW
subsections.description: An approximate-nearest-neighbor index that organizes vectors in layered proximity graphs and searches from coarse upper layers toward detailed lower layers.

subsections.title: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
subsections.description: A workflow design in which a person supplies judgment, correction, approval, or escalation at defined points in an AI-driven process.

subsections.title: Hybrid Retrieval
subsections.description: Retrieval that combines signals from different methods, commonly lexical matching and dense-vector similarity, before merging or reranking results.

subsections.title: Hyperparameter
subsections.description: A configuration choice that shapes model structure, optimization, data processing, or inference rather than being learned as an ordinary model parameter. Examples include learning rate, batch size, layer count, and decoding settings.

subsections.title: Idempotency
subsections.description: The property that repeating the same operation with the same identity does not create additional side effects beyond the first successful application.

subsections.title: Image Token
subsections.description: A model-specific visual unit represented as a vector or discrete code, commonly derived from an image patch, region, or learned visual-codebook entry.

subsections.title: In-Context Learning
subsections.description: A model adapting its behavior from instructions, examples, or patterns supplied in the current input without an ordinary parameter update.

subsections.title: Incident Response
subsections.description: The coordinated process for detecting, analyzing, containing, recovering from, communicating, and learning from an event that threatens service, data, safety, or security.

subsections.title: Indirect Prompt Injection
subsections.description: A prompt-injection attack delivered through content the system retrieves or observes, such as a webpage, document, email, image text, or tool result, rather than directly through the user's instruction.

subsections.title: Inductive Bias
subsections.description: Structural or statistical assumptions that favor some functions or representations over others. Convolution favors locality and shared filters; causal masking favors prediction from preceding positions.

subsections.title: Inference
subsections.description: Executing a trained model to produce predictions, scores, embeddings, or generated tokens without performing an ordinary training update to its parameters.

subsections.title: Instruction Following
subsections.description: A model capability to map natural-language directions and supplied context to behavior that satisfies the stated task and constraints.

subsections.title: Instruction Hierarchy
subsections.description: A rule set for resolving conflicts among instructions from sources with different authority, such as application policy, users, and untrusted retrieved content.

subsections.title: Inter-Token Latency (ITL)
subsections.description: The elapsed time between two consecutive output-token arrival events for one request, calculated as `t_i - t_(i-1)` for an output token after the first.

subsections.title: Jailbreak
subsections.description: An adversarial input or interaction strategy intended to make a model produce behavior that its training or application controls are designed to prevent.

subsections.title: JAX
subsections.description: A Python library for transforming numerical functions with automatic differentiation, compilation, vectorization, and parallel execution across accelerators. Its transformations work best with explicit state and functional-style code.

subsections.title: Knowledge Distillation
subsections.description: Training a student model to reproduce selected behavior or output distributions from a more capable teacher, often alongside ordinary target labels.

subsections.title: KV Cache
subsections.description: Stored key and value tensors from earlier positions in autoregressive generation. Reusing them avoids recomputing attention projections for the unchanged prefix at every decoding step.

subsections.title: Late Fusion
subsections.description: Processing modalities through separate encoders or predictors and combining their high-level representations, scores, or decisions near the task output.

subsections.title: Latent Space
subsections.description: A learned representation space whose coordinates encode factors useful to a model. It may be lower-dimensional than the input, but compression is not required for every latent representation.

subsections.title: Learning Rate
subsections.description: A scale factor used by an optimizer to control parameter-update magnitude. Values that are too large can destabilize training; values that are too small can make useful progress impractically slow.

subsections.title: Learning Rate Schedule
subsections.description: A policy that changes the optimizer's learning rate as training progresses according to steps, epochs, metrics, or a predefined curve.

subsections.title: Least Privilege
subsections.description: Giving a model, agent, tool, or user only the permissions required for the current task, for only as long as those permissions are needed.

subsections.title: LLM (Large Language Model)
subsections.description: A language model with enough capacity and broad training to perform many language tasks through prompting or adaptation. Most current LLMs use transformer architectures and sequence-prediction objectives, but size thresholds, data sources, and training recipes vary.

subsections.title: LLM-as-a-Judge
subsections.description: Using a language model to score, compare, classify, or critique another system's output against a rubric.

subsections.title: Load Shedding
subsections.description: Deliberately rejecting, dropping, or cancelling selected work at one or more overload boundaries when demand exceeds the capacity available to produce useful results.

subsections.title: Logits
subsections.description: The model's unnormalized numeric scores for candidate outcomes before a normalization function or decoding rule converts them into selections.

subsections.title: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
subsections.description: A method that keeps base weights frozen and learns low-rank update matrices for selected layers. It reduces the number of trainable parameters and can lower training memory relative to full-parameter fine-tuning.

subsections.title: Loss Function
subsections.description: An objective that maps predictions and targets, sometimes with regularization terms, to a value optimization tries to reduce. The loss determines which errors training directly rewards or penalizes.

subsections.title: Lost in the Middle
subsections.description: A long-context failure pattern in which model performance changes with evidence position and can degrade when relevant information sits between the beginning and end.

subsections.title: Maximum Marginal Relevance (MMR)
subsections.description: A selection rule that balances relevance to the query with novelty relative to items already selected.

subsections.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
subsections.description: An open JSON-RPC protocol for a host to connect to servers that expose tools, resources, prompts, and extensions through defined request, result, discovery, and transport contracts. In revision 2026-07-28, every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities instead of relying on an initialization handshake or protocol session.

subsections.title: Membership Inference
subsections.description: An attack that estimates whether a particular record or example was included in a model's training data by observing model outputs or other accessible signals.

subsections.title: Mixed Precision
subsections.description: A numerical strategy that uses different data types for different operations, often lower precision for many matrix operations and higher precision for values that need more range or stability.

subsections.title: Modality
subsections.description: A form of information with its own structure and acquisition process, such as text, image, audio, video, depth, or sensor measurements.

subsections.title: Modality Alignment
subsections.description: Learning or establishing correspondences between representations from different modalities so semantically or temporally related items can be matched.

subsections.title: Model Card
subsections.description: A structured report describing a model's intended uses, evaluation conditions, performance characteristics, limitations, and relevant ethical or safety considerations.

subsections.title: Model Router
subsections.description: A component that selects a model or provider for a request using requirements such as capability, latency, cost, context size, policy, and current availability.

subsections.title: Model Serving
subsections.description: The runtime and API layer that loads versioned model artifacts, accepts inference requests, schedules execution, manages resources, and returns results under an operational contract.

subsections.title: MoE (Mixture of Experts)
subsections.description: An architecture with multiple expert subnetworks and a learned router that selects a subset for each input unit, often each token. Sparse activation can increase total parameter capacity without using every expert on every forward pass.

subsections.title: Multimodal Fusion
subsections.description: Combining evidence or learned representations from more than one modality to produce a joint representation, prediction, or generated output.

subsections.title: Multimodal Model
subsections.description: A model that learns from, relates, or generates more than one modality through representation, alignment, fusion, translation, or coordinated prediction.

subsections.title: Multi Round-Trip Request (MRTR)
subsections.description: An MCP request pattern in which an operation returns `resultType: input_required` with one or more `inputRequests`, then the client retries the original method with `inputResponses` and the exact returned `requestState`.

subsections.title: NaN (Not a Number)
subsections.description: A floating-point value representing an undefined or unrepresentable numerical result. In training, NaNs can come from invalid operations, overflow, unstable normalization, excessive updates, or earlier corrupted values.

subsections.title: Normalization
subsections.description: A family of transformations that rescale or recenter inputs, activations, or features using defined statistics. Batch normalization and layer normalization use different axes and behave differently across training and inference.

subsections.title: Nucleus Sampling (Top-p)
subsections.description: A decoding method that samples from the smallest set of next-token candidates whose cumulative probability reaches a chosen threshold.

subsections.title: Observability
subsections.description: The ability to understand an AI system's behavior from recorded inputs, outputs, state transitions, tool calls, timings, costs, errors, and evaluation signals.

subsections.title: Optimizer
subsections.description: An algorithm that transforms gradients into parameter updates. Plain stochastic gradient descent is a simple baseline; momentum, Adam, and other optimizers change the update using history or adaptive scaling. Each choice has different memory, stability, and tuning behavior.

subsections.title: Orchestration
subsections.description: The control logic that sequences, branches, delegates, retries, pauses, resumes, and terminates work across model and tool steps.

subsections.title: Overfitting
subsections.description: A generalization gap in which performance on training data is substantially better than performance on representative unseen data. Memorization can contribute, but the operational symptom is poor generalization.

subsections.title: Paged KV Cache
subsections.description: A KV-cache memory manager that stores attention state in fixed-size blocks and maps logical sequence positions to physical blocks instead of requiring one contiguous allocation per sequence.

subsections.title: Parameter
subsections.description: A value learned during training, commonly a weight, bias, embedding element, or normalization parameter. Parameter count is one measure of model capacity, but it does not directly determine quality, memory, or serving cost.

subsections.title: Pass@k
subsections.description: Across a task set, the fraction of tasks for which at least one of k sampled candidates passes a defined correctness test.

subsections.title: Patch
subsections.description: A reviewable representation of changes to one or more files, usually expressed as additions and deletions against a known base revision.

subsections.title: Patch Embedding
subsections.description: A learned projection that converts an image patch into a fixed-width vector used as one element of a transformer input sequence.

subsections.title: Perplexity
subsections.description: The exponentiated average negative log-likelihood under a stated tokenization and logarithm convention. Lower values mean the model assigned higher probability to the evaluated sequence.

subsections.title: Pipeline Parallelism
subsections.description: Partitioning sequential groups of model layers across devices and moving microbatches or requests through those stages as a pipeline.

subsections.title: Planning
subsections.description: Constructing, selecting, or revising a sequence of actions and dependencies intended to move from the current state to a goal.

subsections.title: Postmortem
subsections.description: A durable incident record that explains impact, detection, response, contributing conditions, recovery, and owned follow-up actions without assigning blame as a substitute for analysis.

subsections.title: Precision & Recall
subsections.description: Precision asks how many flagged items were correct; recall asks how many relevant items were found. When you change the decision threshold for one fixed scoring model, improving recall often lowers precision and vice versa. A better model can improve both. F1 is their harmonic mean.

subsections.title: Prefill
subsections.description: The initial inference stage that processes all supplied input tokens to produce their representations and the attention state required for subsequent autoregressive generation.

subsections.title: Prefix Caching
subsections.description: Reusing KV-cache blocks produced for an identical eligible token prefix across requests so the serving runtime can skip repeated prefix computation.

subsections.title: Progressive Disclosure
subsections.description: Supplying a person or model with the minimum useful context first, then revealing deeper detail when the task or evidence requires it.

subsections.title: Prompt Cache
subsections.description: Reuse of provider-side or application-side computation for an identical or eligible prompt prefix so repeated inference avoids some preprocessing work.

subsections.title: Prompt Engineering
subsections.description: Designing model-facing instructions, examples, constraints, and output requirements to improve behavior on a defined task.

subsections.title: Prompt Injection
subsections.description: An attack or failure mode in which untrusted content influences a model to disregard intended instructions, expose data, misuse tools, or take actions outside the user's goal. The content can arrive directly from a user or indirectly through retrieved pages, files, messages, or tool output.

subsections.title: Prompt Sensitivity
subsections.description: Variation in model output or measured performance caused by changes to prompt wording, order, formatting, or examples that preserve the intended task.

subsections.title: Provenance Attestation
subsections.description: Authenticated, machine-readable metadata that binds an artifact to claims about how, where, when, and from which inputs it was produced.

subsections.title: Purpose Limitation
subsections.description: For personal data, collecting and using it only for specified, explicit purposes unless a new use has an appropriate compatible or authorized basis.

subsections.title: QLoRA
subsections.description: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that keeps a pretrained base model frozen in a low-bit quantized representation while training LoRA adapters with higher-precision computation where needed.

subsections.title: Quantization
subsections.description: Representing weights, activations, or caches with lower-precision formats to reduce memory, bandwidth, or compute cost. Methods differ in calibration, granularity, data type, and whether conversion happens before, during, or after training.

subsections.title: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
subsections.description: A system pattern that retrieves evidence relevant to a request and supplies selected content to a generative model before it answers or acts. Retrieval can use lexical, vector, structured, or hybrid methods.

subsections.title: Rate Limit
subsections.description: A policy that caps requests, tokens, concurrent work, or another resource within a defined time or capacity window.

subsections.title: ReAct
subsections.description: An agent pattern that interleaves task reasoning, a concrete action, and an observation returned by the environment before deciding the next step.

subsections.title: Readiness Probe
subsections.description: A diagnostic that tells the traffic-routing layer whether a service instance is currently able to accept requests.

subsections.title: Recall@K
subsections.description: For one query, Recall@K is `|relevant items intersecting the top k| / |relevant items|`. A dataset score aggregates those per-query values under a stated rule.

subsections.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
subsections.description: A rank-fusion method that combines several result lists by summing contributions that decrease with each item's rank in each list.

subsections.title: Red Teaming
subsections.description: A structured adversarial testing process in which authorized testers seek failures using documented objectives, threat assumptions, cases, and evidence.

subsections.title: Regression Test
subsections.description: A repeatable check that protects behavior known to work, especially after code, prompt, model, retrieval, or tool changes.

subsections.title: ReLU
subsections.description: Rectified Linear Unit, defined as `f(x) = max(0, x)`. It is inexpensive and has a non-saturating positive branch, though zero gradients on negative inputs can create inactive units.

subsections.title: Repository Instructions
subsections.description: Version-controlled guidance that tells coding agents how a repository is organized, which commands and conventions apply, what boundaries to respect, and how to verify work.

subsections.title: Repository Map
subsections.description: A compact, maintained description of a repository's important directories, ownership boundaries, entry points, build commands, tests, generated files, and local instructions.

subsections.title: Reproducible Build
subsections.description: A build whose declared source, environment, and instructions can be independently rerun to produce bit-for-bit identical specified artifacts.

subsections.title: Reranker
subsections.description: A second-stage model or scoring function that reorders a small candidate set using a richer comparison between the query and each candidate.

subsections.title: Retry Budget
subsections.description: A bound on retry traffic, usually expressed relative to original requests or over a time window, that prevents retries from consuming unbounded capacity.

subsections.title: Retry with Backoff
subsections.description: Repeating a failed transient operation after progressively longer delays, usually with randomized jitter and a strict retry limit.

subsections.title: Reviewer Agent
subsections.description: An agent assigned to inspect another agent's artifact or decision against explicit criteria and return findings or a verdict.

subsections.title: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)
subsections.description: A family of pipelines that uses human feedback to learn a reward or preference signal and then optimizes a model policy against that signal. Implementations vary and need not all use the same reinforcement-learning algorithm.

subsections.title: Rollback
subsections.description: Restoring a previously known deployment or configuration when the current release violates operational, quality, or safety criteria.

subsections.title: ROUGE
subsections.description: A family of metrics that compares generated text with reference text using units such as n-gram overlap or longest common subsequence.

subsections.title: Sandbox
subsections.description: An isolated execution environment that restricts an agent's access to files, processes, network destinations, credentials, and host resources.

subsections.title: Saturation
subsections.description: The degree to which a constrained resource or service has exhausted its capacity, including queued work that cannot begin promptly.

subsections.title: Scope Contract
subsections.description: A concrete agreement that defines a task's goal, allowed and forbidden surfaces, expected artifacts, verification requirements, and stopping conditions.

subsections.title: Self-Attention
subsections.description: Attention in which queries, keys, and values are derived from the same sequence representation. Scaled similarity scores are normalized and used to combine values, subject to causal, padding, local, or other masks.

subsections.title: Semantic Cache
subsections.description: A cache that reuses a previous result when a new request is judged sufficiently similar under a chosen representation and threshold.

subsections.title: Semantic Search
subsections.description: Retrieval that represents a query and candidates in an embedding space and ranks candidates using a vector-similarity function.

subsections.title: Separation of Duties
subsections.description: Dividing conflicting responsibilities or authority across independent roles so one principal cannot complete a high-risk action without another authorized decision.

subsections.title: Service Level Indicator (SLI)
subsections.description: A quantitative measure of service behavior at a defined user-relevant boundary, such as successful request ratio or latency below a threshold.

subsections.title: Service Level Objective (SLO)
subsections.description: A target range or threshold for a service-level indicator over a stated population and measurement window.

subsections.title: SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning)
subsections.description: Fine-tuning a pretrained model on paired inputs and desired responses so it learns the demonstrated behavior under the training distribution.

subsections.title: Shadow Traffic
subsections.description: A copy of live request traffic sent to a candidate system for observation while the candidate response remains outside the primary user response path. Because the copied request still executes, its side effects must be isolated.

subsections.title: Shared Embedding Space
subsections.description: A common vector space in which representations from different modalities can be compared with the same similarity function.

subsections.title: Skill Bundle
subsections.description: The complete installable skill directory, including `SKILL.md` and every reference, script, asset, fixture, or companion file required by the workflow.

subsections.title: Skill Catalog
subsections.description: The compact model-visible inventory of eligible skills, usually containing routing metadata such as name, description, and an internal source identifier rather than every skill body.

subsections.title: Skill Discovery
subsections.description: A runtime pipeline that searches configured roots, identifies candidate skill directories, validates their package contract, attaches scope and provenance, resolves collisions, and publishes eligible catalog entries.

subsections.title: Skill Invocation
subsections.description: The runtime-mediated process in which an eligible human, model, application, or other skill selects a skill and causes its instructions to enter the working context.

subsections.title: Softmax
subsections.description: A function defined by `softmax(x_i) = exp(x_i) / sum(exp(x_j))`, implemented with numerical stabilization. Its outputs are positive and sum to one, so they can parameterize a categorical distribution.

subsections.title: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
subsections.description: A structured inventory of software components and relationships associated with a product or artifact, often including versions, suppliers, licenses, and identifiers.

subsections.title: Speculative Decoding
subsections.description: An inference method in which a cheaper draft process proposes several tokens and the target model scores those draft positions in parallel. In exact sampling variants, an acceptance and correction rule preserves the target model's output distribution.

subsections.title: Stateless MCP
subsections.description: The MCP 2026-07-28 request model in which every request carries the protocol version and client capabilities in `params._meta`, while results carry an explicit `resultType`; no protocol state is keyed by an initialization handshake, connection, or `Mcp-Session-Id`.

subsections.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD)
subsections.description: An optimizer family that updates parameters from a gradient estimated on a sampled example or minibatch rather than the complete training dataset.

subsections.title: Stop Sequence
subsections.description: An application-specified token or text pattern that causes generation to stop when the decoding system encounters it.

subsections.title: Streaming
subsections.description: Delivering incremental response events before the complete result is ready. A stream may contain token text, structured deltas, tool-call arguments, usage metadata, or status events depending on the API.

subsections.title: Structured Output
subsections.description: Model output constrained or validated against a machine-readable schema so application code can consume fields without parsing free-form prose.

subsections.title: Swarm
subsections.description: A loosely coordinated multi-agent pattern in which local agent decisions and message exchange produce system-level behavior. The term is used inconsistently, so the actual topology, state ownership, and termination rules must be specified.

subsections.title: System Prompt
subsections.description: A provider-defined instruction message or configuration supplied by the application to establish behavior and constraints within that provider's instruction hierarchy.

subsections.title: Tail Latency
subsections.description: The latency experienced by the slowest portion of requests, commonly summarized with a high percentile under a stated workload and time window.

subsections.title: Temperature
subsections.description: A decoding parameter that rescales logits before a probability distribution is formed. Higher positive values usually flatten the distribution; lower positive values sharpen it.

subsections.title: Tensor
subsections.description: A typed array with a shape, data type, and device placement that frameworks use to represent inputs, parameters, activations, and gradients. Automatic-differentiation metadata is framework- and operation-dependent, not an inherent property of every tensor.

subsections.title: Tensor Parallelism
subsections.description: Partitioning tensor operations within a model layer across devices, with collective communication combining partial results during the layer computation.

subsections.title: Termination Condition
subsections.description: An explicit rule that ends or pauses an agent run when it succeeds, fails, exhausts a budget, reaches a safe boundary, or requires escalation.

subsections.title: Test Oracle
subsections.description: The mechanism, specification, reference, invariant, or human judgment used to decide whether observed program behavior is correct.

subsections.title: Threat Model
subsections.description: A documented account of protected assets, trust boundaries, potential adversaries, assumed capabilities, attack paths, impacts, and planned controls.

subsections.title: Time per Output Token (TPOT)
subsections.description: For one request with `N > 1` output tokens, the average post-first-token interval: `(t_N - t_1) / (N - 1)`. System distributions then aggregate those per-request averages.

subsections.title: Time to First Token (TTFT)
subsections.description: The elapsed time from submitting a generation request until the client receives the first output token or content event under a defined measurement boundary.

subsections.title: Token
subsections.description: An integer identifier produced by a model-specific tokenizer from text, bytes, images, audio, or another input representation. A token can be a whole word, part of a word, punctuation, whitespace, a byte sequence, or a special control symbol.

subsections.title: Token Budget
subsections.description: An explicit allocation of token capacity across instructions, evidence, history, tool results, reasoning or working space, and output.

subsections.title: Tokenization
subsections.description: Converting an input representation into the ordered token identifiers a specific model or tokenizer accepts.

subsections.title: Tokens per Second (TPS)
subsections.description: A throughput measure reporting how many output tokens a serving system produces per unit time under a stated scope and workload.

subsections.title: Tool Contract
subsections.description: The complete agreement for a tool boundary: purpose, typed inputs, outputs, validation, permissions, side effects, errors, timeouts, idempotency, and evidence returned to the caller.

subsections.title: Top-k Sampling
subsections.description: A decoding method that restricts the next-token distribution to the k highest-scoring candidates, renormalizes their probabilities, and samples from that set.

subsections.title: Trace
subsections.description: A correlated record of one request or task across model calls, retrieval, tools, state transitions, retries, approvals, and evaluations.

subsections.title: Transfer Learning
subsections.description: Starting from representations or parameters learned on one data distribution or objective and adapting them for another. The transferable components and update strategy depend on architecture and task.

subsections.title: Transformer
subsections.description: A neural-network architecture built from attention, position information, feed-forward sublayers, residual connections, and normalization. Encoder, decoder, and encoder-decoder variants use different masks and information flows.

subsections.title: Trust Boundary
subsections.description: An interface where data, instructions, identity, or authority crosses between components or principals that operate under different trust assumptions.

subsections.title: Underfitting
subsections.description: A model or training setup has insufficient effective capacity, optimization, features, or training signal to capture useful patterns in the training data.

subsections.title: VAE (Variational Autoencoder)
subsections.description: A latent-variable model trained with a reconstruction objective and a regularization term that keeps an approximate posterior close to a chosen prior. The reparameterization estimator allows gradients through stochastic latent sampling.

subsections.title: Vector Database
subsections.description: A storage and indexing system that supports nearest-neighbor queries over vector representations, often with metadata filtering, persistence, and approximate indexes.

subsections.title: Verification Gate
subsections.description: A control point that blocks progress until defined evidence satisfies a correctness or quality criterion.

subsections.title: Vision-Language Model (VLM)
subsections.description: A model that learns relationships between, or jointly processes, visual and language representations for tasks such as retrieval, description, question answering, or grounded generation.

subsections.title: Vision Transformer (ViT)
subsections.description: A vision architecture that represents an image as a sequence of patch embeddings with position information and processes that sequence with transformer encoder blocks.

subsections.title: Visual Grounding
subsections.description: Connecting a language expression to spatial evidence in an image or video, such as a region, object, mask, or tracked entity.

subsections.title: Vocabulary
subsections.description: The finite mapping between token identifiers and the units a tokenizer can emit, including ordinary, byte-level, and special control tokens.

subsections.title: Warmup
subsections.description: An initial training phase in which the learning rate rises from a smaller value toward the main schedule's target value.

subsections.title: Weight
subsections.description: A trainable coefficient in a model transformation. Weights are usually organized into tensors, and optimization adjusts them to reduce the training objective.

subsections.title: Weight Decay
subsections.description: An update rule that reduces selected parameter magnitudes over training, often by multiplying weights by a shrinkage factor separate from the gradient update.

subsections.title: Worktree
subsections.description: In Git, a working directory attached to a repository and branch or commit, with shared object storage but its own checked-out files and index.

subsections.title: Zero-Shot
subsections.description: Performing a task from instructions or task framing without including task-specific demonstrations in the immediate input.

subsections.title: Zero Trust
subsections.description: A security model that grants no implicit trust from network location or asset ownership and instead evaluates each access request against identity, device, resource, policy, and current context.

items.description: Zombie process: child has completed execution (exit status stored in process table) but parent has not called wait() to reap it; consumes PID entries. items.title: FCFS / SJF / SRTF

SRTF (Shortest Remaining Time First): preemptive SJF, preemption occurs if a new arrival has a shorter remaining burst.

items.title: Round Robin

items.title: TCP 3-way handshake

items.title: HTTP anatomy (req/resp)
items.description: Stateless client-server protocol. Request: HTTP Method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS), URI path, headers (Host, User-Agent, Content-Type, Authorization), and optional payload body. Response: Status Code (1xx Info, 2xx Success, 3xx Redirect, 4xx Client Error, 5xx Server Error), response headers, and payload.

items.title: HTTP/1.1 vs 2 vs 3
items.description: HTTP/1.1: textual protocol, keep-alive persistent connections, pipelining suffered from severe Head-of-Line blocking. HTTP/2: binary framing layer, multiplexed bidirectional streams over a single TCP connection, HPACK header compression, server push (TCP HOL blocking persists on packet loss). HTTP/3: built on UDP/QUIC, eliminates TCP HOL blocking, integrates TLS 1.3 0-RTT, and enables instant connection migration.

items.title: DNS resolution flow
items.description: Hierarchical name resolution: Browser Cache -> OS Resolver Cache (hosts file) -> Recursive DNS Resolver (ISP/Cloudflare 1.1.1.1/Google 8.8.8.8) -> Root Nameservers ('.') -> TLD Nameservers ('.com') -> Authoritative Nameservers ('example.com'). Recursive resolver caches responses adhering to TTL directives.

items.title: DNS records (A, CNAME, MX, TXT)
items.description: Core DNS zone records: A (maps hostname to IPv4 address), AAAA (maps to 128-bit IPv6 address), CNAME (canonical name alias pointing to another hostname, cannot coexist with other records at zone apex), ALIAS/ANAME (virtual CNAME resolved at apex by DNS server), MX (mail exchange records with priority weights), TXT (arbitrary text; critical for SPF, DKIM, and domain ownership verification).

items.title: DNS caching
items.description: Multi-tier caching hierarchy minimizing DNS lookup latency (which costs 20-120ms). Governed by Time-To-Live (TTL) field set by domain administrators. High TTL (86400s) maximizes cache hit rates and reduces resolver load; low TTL (60s) enables rapid failover during migrations or disaster recovery events.

items.title: TLS handshake (1.2 vs 1.3)
items.description: Cryptographic transport layer security. TLS 1.2 requires 2 full round-trips (2-RTT) to negotiate cipher suites, exchange key parameters (RSA/Diffie-Hellman), and verify certificates. TLS 1.3 cuts handshake latency to 1-RTT (and 0-RTT Early Data for resumed sessions) by mandating Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (PFS) and deprecating insecure legacy ciphers (RC4, 3DES, MD5, SHA-1).

items.title: Certificates & PKI
items.description: Public Key Infrastructure: enables trust without prior communication. Servers present an X.509 certificate signed by an intermediate Certificate Authority (CA), forming a cryptographic chain of trust validated against Root CA certificates pre-installed in the client OS trust store. Mutual TLS (mTLS) enforces two-way verification where clients must also present certificates to authenticate microservices.

items.title: HSTS, OCSP stapling
items.description: HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security): response header instructing browsers to automatically upgrade all insecure HTTP requests to HTTPS for a declared duration (e.g. max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload), thwarting SSL-stripping attacks. OCSP Stapling: server periodically queries CA for signed revocation status and staples it directly to the TLS handshake, eliminating client-side OCSP blocking latency and privacy leaks.

items.title: JOIN types
items.description: Relational algebra set operations. INNER JOIN: returns rows with matching keys in both tables. LEFT/RIGHT OUTER JOIN: preserves all rows from left/right table, populating unmatched columns with NULL. FULL OUTER JOIN: preserves all rows from both tables. CROSS JOIN: Cartesian product (N × M rows). In query engines, implemented via Nested Loop Join (O(M×N), fast with index), Hash Join (O(M+N), builds in-memory hash table for large unindexed datasets), or Sort-Merge Join (O(M log M + N log N), optimal for pre-sorted inputs).

items.title: GROUP BY + aggregates
items.description: Data summarization operations. GROUP BY partitions rows sharing identical grouping keys. Aggregates (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX) compute scalar metrics per group. Critical interview distinction: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping occurs; HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY evaluation.

items.title: Window functions
items.description: Computes aggregate-like calculations across a subset ('window') of rows while preserving individual row identities (unlike GROUP BY which collapses rows). Syntax: `OVER (PARTITION BY... ORDER BY...)`. Includes ranking (ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), DENSE_RANK()), offset navigation (LAG(), LEAD()), and cumulative running totals (SUM() OVER (...)).

items.title: CTEs (WITH)
items.description: Common Table Expressions (WITH clause): defines temporary named result sets scoped to the execution of a single query, significantly improving SQL readability and modularity over deeply nested subqueries. Recursive CTEs enable traversal of hierarchical and graph structures (e.g. organizational charts, bill-of-materials, ancestor trees).

items.title: Subqueries vs JOINs
items.description: Non-correlated subqueries execute once, allowing optimizer substitution. Correlated subqueries reference outer query columns and evaluate repeatedly for every outer row (O(N×M) penalty if unindexed). Modern cost-based optimizers rewrite subqueries into equivalent JOINs or semi-joins (EXISTS/IN) to leverage index scans and hash joins.

items.title: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF
items.description: Systematic database design reducing data redundancy and preventing update anomalies. 1NF: atomic column values, unique rows (primary key). 2NF: 1NF + no partial dependency (all non-key attributes fully dependent on whole candidate key). 3NF: 2NF + no transitive dependencies (non-key attributes depend only on the primary key). BCNF (Boyce-Codd): stricter 3NF where every determinant must be a candidate key.

items.title: Denormalization tradeoffs
items.description: Deliberate introduction of controlled redundancy into normalized schemas (e.g. precomputed totals, duplicate customer names in order tables) to eliminate expensive multi-table JOINs and reduce read latency in read-heavy applications. Trade-offs: increased storage footprint, higher write latency (write amplification), and severe risk of data inconsistency requiring distributed transactions or background reconciliation jobs.

items.title: B-Tree vs Hash vs GIN/GiST
items.description: Index data structures. B+ Tree: self-balancing search tree with high fanout (100-500) and low depth (3-4); stores records/pointers only in leaf nodes connected via doubly linked list, optimizing range scans and equality lookups. Hash Index: O(1) equality lookups, but completely incapable of range queries or sorting. GIN (Generalized Inverted Index): maps components (JSON keys, full-text words, array elements) to row pointers, essential for document and full-text search.

items.title: Clustered vs non-clustered
items.description: Clustered Index: dictates the physical ordering of table rows on disk; leaf pages contain the actual table data rows (only 1 clustered index permitted per table, typically the Primary Key). Non-Clustered (Secondary) Index: independent B+ tree structure whose leaf nodes contain index keys and a pointer/primary key to the physical data row; secondary queries require a secondary lookup ('bookmark lookup') unless all requested columns exist in the index ('Covering Index').

items.title: Composite + leftmost prefix
items.description: Multi-column index (e.g. index on (A, B, C)). Governed by the Leftmost Prefix Rule: queries can utilize the index for filtering if they constrain the leading column (A), (A, B), or (A, B, C). Queries filtering on (B) or (C) alone cannot navigate the tree root and result in a full index/table scan.

items.title: Index selectivity & cardinality
items.description: Cardinality: the count of distinct values in a column. Selectivity: the ratio of distinct values to total rows (`cardinality / total_rows`). High selectivity (~1.0, e.g. UUID, email, user_id) makes an index extremely efficient. Low selectivity (e.g. boolean flags, gender status) causes query optimizers to bypass the index in favor of a sequential table scan because random disk I/O from index lookups costs more than sequential reading.

items.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE
items.description: Query profiling commands. EXPLAIN outputs the query execution plan generated by the cost-based optimizer (showing anticipated cost, estimated rows, and selected join/scan operators). EXPLAIN ANALYZE actually executes the query and reports real runtime execution times, actual row counts, memory/buffer usage, and disk spill metrics (identifying Seq Scans, nested loops, and temporary disk sorts).

items.title: ACID
items.description: Atomicity: all operations in a transaction succeed together or rollback completely via Write-Ahead Log (WAL) or undo logs. Consistency: transactions transition database from one valid state to another, satisfying all schema constraints, foreign keys, and triggers. Isolation: concurrent transactions execute without interfering with one another. Durability: committed changes persist through crashes and power loss via fsync to non-volatile storage.

items.title: Isolation levels
items.description: ANSI SQL Isolation Levels: Read Uncommitted (allows dirty reads, no read locks), Read Committed (prevents dirty reads, reads latest committed snapshot per statement), Repeatable Read (prevents non-repeatable reads, reads snapshot taken at transaction start), Serializable (highest isolation, guarantees concurrent execution is equivalent to some serial ordering).

items.title: Anomalies (dirty/non-repeatable/phantom)
items.description: Concurrency anomalies. Dirty Read: reading uncommitted data written by a concurrent transaction that later rolls back. Non-repeatable (Fuzzy) Read: re-reading the same row returns modified column values committed by another transaction. Phantom Read: re-executing a range query returns newly inserted/deleted rows matching the predicate. Write Skew: concurrent transactions read overlapping data, make disjoint modifications, and commit invalid state violating cross-row constraints.

items.title: MVCC
items.description: Multi-Version Concurrency Control: concurrent transactions see point-in-time consistent snapshots without blocking writers, and writers do not block readers. Implemented via row versioning: PostgreSQL appends new tuple versions with `xmin`/`xmax` transaction IDs and reclaims dead tuples via VACUUM; MySQL InnoDB modifies rows in-place in clustered index pages and stores previous versions in an Undo Log rollback segment.

items.title: Locks & deadlock
items.description: Locking mechanisms: Shared Locks (S-locks, read locks, multiple concurrent holders) and Exclusive Locks (X-locks, write locks, single holder). Deadlock occurs when two or more transactions hold locks the other needs in a circular wait dependency (e.g., T1 holds A, waits for B; T2 holds B, waits for A). Resolved by engine via Deadlock Detection (wait-for graph cycle hunting and aborting the cheapest victim transaction) or Deadlock Prevention (wait-die or wound-wait timestamp schemes).

items.title: Optimistic concurrency
items.description: Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC): transactions execute reads and writes without acquiring locks under the assumption that conflicts are rare. Upon commit, the transaction validates whether data changed during its execution (typically by verifying a `version` integer column or timestamp). If conflicted, the transaction aborts and retries. Superior throughput for read-heavy, low-contention workloads.

items.description: Stores semi-structured data as JSON/BSON documents with dynamic, flexible schemas (MongoDB, Couchbase). Allows embedding child entities (e.g. order items inside order document) to enable atomic single-document reads without joins. Ideal for catalogs, content management, and rapidly evolving domain models.

items.title: Key-Value (Redis)
items.description: High-performance data store associating opaque or structured data values with unique string keys (Redis, Memcached, DynamoDB). In-memory engines deliver sub-millisecond latencies using single-threaded event loops (Redis) and specialized in-memory data structures (Hashes, Sorted Sets, Bitmaps, HyperLogLogs). Employs persistence strategies: RDB snapshots and AOF (Append-Only File) journals.

items.title: Wide-column (Cassandra)
items.description: Distributed column-family architecture derived from Google Bigtable (Apache Cassandra, ScyllaDB). Organizes data by Partition Key (hashed via consistent hashing to locate replica nodes) and Clustering Key (determines physical on-disk sort order within the partition). Powered by LSM-Trees; excels at high-throughput write-intensive workloads, time-series data, and petabyte-scale horizontal scaling with tunable consistency (QUORUM).

items.title: Graph (Neo4j)

items.title: Amdahl's Law
items.description: Theoretical formula bounding maximum speedup S = 1 / ((1-p) + p/N), where p is the parallelizable fraction of the task and N is the number of processor cores. Demonstrates that even with infinite cores (N -> inf), maximum speedup is strictly capped by the serial fraction 1/(1-p) (e.g., if 5% of code is sequential, max theoretical speedup is 20x). Contrasted with Gustafson's Law for scaling problem sizes.

items.title: Mutex
items.description: Mutual Exclusion lock: guarantees that only a single thread can execute inside a designated critical section at any given moment. Blocking mutexes (e.g. pthread_mutex) place contending threads into an OS sleep queue via the Linux futex syscall. Critical trade-off: prevents race conditions but incurs context switch overhead (~1-2µs) when contention occurs.

items.title: Semaphore
items.description: Signaling mechanism maintaining an internal integer counter protected by atomics. Counting Semaphore: initialized to N permits, allowing up to N concurrent threads into a resource pool (e.g. database connection pool, rate limiter). Binary Semaphore: permit count 0 or 1, similar to a mutex but differs fundamentally: a semaphore has no concept of ownership (thread A can post/release a semaphore acquired by thread B).

items.title: Condition variable
items.description: Signaling primitive enabling threads to suspend execution (sleep) until notified that a specific application state condition has become true (paired with an associated mutex). Always requires checking the condition inside a while loop (never if) to guard against Spurious Wakeups (waking without explicit signal) and race conditions before lock reacquisition.

items.title: Read-write lock
items.description: Reader-Writer Lock (Shared-Exclusive lock): allows unlimited simultaneous reader threads (Shared lock) or exactly one writer thread (Exclusive lock). Drastically boosts read throughput in read-heavy workloads (e.g., routing tables, config caches). Must be carefully designed to prevent Writer Starvation (continuous incoming readers blocking a pending writer) using fair queueing or write-preference policies.

items.title: Spinlock
items.description: Spinlock: contending threads repeatedly execute a tight CPU polling loop ('spin') testing an atomic flag instead of yielding the CPU. Optimal only when the critical section is extremely brief (< context switch latency ~1µs) and on multi-core systems; disastrous on single-core or long-running sections as it burns 100% CPU.

items.title: Deadlock (4 conditions)
items.description: Permanent stall where two or more threads cannot proceed because each is waiting for a resource held by another. Four Coffman Conditions must hold simultaneously: 1. Eliminating any single condition prevents deadlock (most commonly breaking Circular Wait via strict total ordering of lock acquisition).

items.title: Producer-Consumer

items.title: Dining Philosophers
items.description: Classic synchronization problem by Dijkstra: 5 philosophers sit at a table with 5 forks; each requires 2 adjacent forks to eat. Naive approach (each picks left fork, waits for right) causes circular deadlock. Solutions: Resource Hierarchy (number forks 1..5, always acquire lowest-numbered fork first), Arbitrator/Waiter (mutex restricting at most 4 philosophers to table), or Chandy/Misra distributed algorithm.

items.title: Branch prediction
items.description: Microarchitectural mechanism that predicts the outcome and target of conditional branch instructions before they are evaluated, keeping the instruction pipeline full. items.title: Cache coherence (MESI)
items.description: Hardware protocol ensuring uniform memory views across multi-core private caches. The MESI protocol categorizes cache lines (typically 64 bytes) into 4 states: Modified (dirty, exclusively cached), Exclusive (clean, exclusively cached), Shared (clean, present in multiple caches), and Invalid. Writes to a shared line broadcast invalidation requests over the bus/interconnect to keep caches coherent.

items.title: Spatial vs temporal locality

items.title: Q: Tell me about a time you had to make a quick decision with incomplete data.
items.description: Situation: Production outage at 2 AM: distributed search cluster nodes were dropping out of consensus, causing search failures; logs showed mixed signals between disk I/O bottlenecks and JVM garbage collection thrashing. Task: Diagnose and restore cluster availability rapidly despite conflicting metrics. Action: Formulated hypothesis that unindexed wild-card queries were triggering full heap allocations, inducing stop-the-world GC pauses that caused Raft heartbeat timeouts; rejected team proposal to reboot all nodes (which would cause cold-cache collapse); instead isolated the traffic spike via ingress rate-limiting and applied a targeted query filter. Result: Cluster stabilized within 7 minutes with zero data loss; post-mortem root cause confirmed GC pause exceeded the 2.5s Raft election threshold.

items.description: Situation: Our Go backend services began suffering unexplained 40ms latency spikes in Kubernetes that internal profilers could not capture because the kernel was descheduling pods. Task: Uncover kernel-level bottlenecks without prior Linux kernel profiling experience. Action: Self-taught eBPF (Extended Berkeley Packet Filter) and BCC tools over a weekend; wrote a custom eBPF tracepoint probe (`runqlat`) to monitor Linux scheduler runqueue latency directly in the kernel; discovered CPU CFS quota throttling was starving threads despite low average CPU usage. Result: Disabled CFS bandwidth quotas in favor of CPU pinning, instantly erasing the 40ms tail latency spike; presented an internal eBPF workshop for 60+ engineers.
